test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 16 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Two taps can fill a cistern in 2 hours and 64 hours, respectively. A third tap can empty it in 2 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill half of the empty cistern, if all of them are opened together?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net rate of filling = Filling Tap 1 + Filling Tap 2 − Emptying Tap 3

Net rate = 1/2 + 1/64 − 1/2 = 1/64 cistern per hour.

Time to fill full cistern = 64 hours.

Time to fill half cistern = 64 ÷ 2 = 32 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 32 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time Tap A = 2 hours, Filling time Tap B = 64 hours, Emptying time Tap C = 2 hours.

**Formula:** Total Work = LCM of time; Efficiency = Work ÷ Time.

⇒ Total efficiency when all taps are open = 32 + 1 − 32 = 1 unit/hour.

⇒ Half of the empty cistern = 64 ÷ 2 = 32 units.

⇒ Time required = 32 units ÷ 1 unit/hour = 32 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 32 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Negative Efficiency

An emptying tap or a leak is always considered to have **negative efficiency** as it reduces the total amount of water in the cistern.

Net Filling Time

If multiple taps are working together, the combined rate is the algebraic sum of their individual rates: (1/Tₜₒₜₐₗ) = (1/T₁) + (1/T₂) − (1/T₃).

LCM Method for Partial Work

When asked for half or any fraction of the tank, simply multiply the **Total Work** (LCM) by that fraction before dividing by net efficiency.</p
